title: 34.2 A 380μW and -242.8dB FoM Digital-PLL-Based GFSK Modulator with Sub-20μs Settling Frequency Hopping for Bluetooth Low-Energy in 22nm CMOS
problem: Ultra-low-power Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) transceivers must support GFSK modulation and adaptive frequency hopping (2.402-2.480GHz) with sub-20μs settling time while minimizing power dissipation, but existing DPLL-based approaches struggle with the power/noise/hopping-speed trade-off.
motivation: Battery-powered IoT nodes, sensors, and wearables demand ULP BLE transceiver designs that simultaneously achieve rapid frequency hopping and low FSK error.
method: The design uses a digital phase-locked loop with a digitally controlled oscillator, or DCO—an oscillator whose frequency you adjust with digital signals. By tracking how the DCO's frequency responds to its control inputs (dynamic-tuning-curve tracking), it encodes data via frequency shifts (GFSK modulation) and hops quickly between Bluetooth channels (2.402-2.480GHz) in under 20 microseconds while adapting to manufacturing and operating variations. It cuts power by using fewer switched-capacitor banks—circuits that switch capacitors on and off to tune frequency—which reduces the energy spent on capacitor switching. The result is 380 microwatts of power consumption with -242.8dB efficiency.
key_novelty: The key innovation is achieving fast frequency hopping with fewer tuning capacitors in the oscillator (a shrunk switched-capacitor bank) by reliably tracking how the oscillator's frequency responds to its control inputs.
contributions: Sub-20μs frequency-hopping settling time for BLE adaptive frequency hopping
22nm CMOS integration supporting full GFSK modulation and AFH within power budget
limitations: BER performance metrics and detailed link-budget analysis not discussed.
